description: Staff-provided ground-truth question set for T6's RAG configuration comparison. Every expected_source and expected_answer below was pulled directly from the files in eval/sample_data/ — check a question against its source file if anything looks off. Ingest sample_data/ into a course (via the file-upload fallback path from T4) before running the comparison harness against these.

questions.question: How many slip days does each student get, and what do they cover?
questions.expected_answer: Each student has a bank of 5 slip days for the semester, usable on P1–P4 only (not the Final Project). Slip days waive the late deduction but never move the hard cutoff.

questions.question: What is the hard cutoff for late project submissions, even if I have slip days left?
questions.expected_answer: No submission is accepted more than 2 days after the due date, for any project, regardless of slip days remaining. Slip days waive the deduction within that window — they don't extend the window itself.

questions.question: Is AI allowed during exams?
questions.expected_answer: No — quizzes and written exams are closed-AI, closed-book. Using AI on them violates the AI Use Policy.

questions.question: By Lecture 13, how many services does the Docker Compose stack have, and what got added?
questions.expected_answer: The stack grows from 3 to 6 services — Ollama (generation), Infinity (embeddings), and ChromaDB (vector store) are the three added at Lecture 13.

questions.question: What is broken in the Project 1 starter code that students have to fix?
questions.expected_answer: The parallax background scrolling system is broken. Background layers should scroll correctly relative to the camera and player movement: the farthest-back layer should be the smallest image and scroll slowest; the layer closest to the tiles should be the largest image and scroll fastest.

questions.question: What checks does Project 2's CI pipeline run before a merge request can be approved?
questions.expected_source_section: T2 — Keep the CI Pipeline Green
questions.expected_answer: Python style (ruff check backend/ scripts/), frontend type checking (tsc --noEmit on all three apps), and GitLab's built-in secret detection scan.

questions.question: In Buzzer's real-time architecture, where does the live game state live versus the permanent record of what happened?
questions.expected_answer: Redis holds the ephemeral live state (current question, who has answered, scores) — fast, per-room, expires with the room. MySQL holds the permanent record — every answer is written to the database immediately.

questions.question: What does temperature control in a language model's output, and what happens near temperature 0 versus above 1.5?
questions.expected_answer: Temperature controls how the model's probability distribution over the vocabulary gets sampled. Near 0.0 is nearly deterministic (the highest-probability token); around 0.7 is balanced with some variety while staying coherent; 1.5 and above is high randomness, more likely to go off the rails.

questions.question: Is a language model fully deterministic at temperature 0?
questions.expected_answer: No. Even at temperature 0.0, the same prompt can produce slightly different output across runs on different hardware, because parallelized floating-point matrix operations aren't perfectly associative — tiny rounding differences can flip which token is technically highest-probability in a near-tie.

questions.question: Does a token count from one model's tokenizer transfer to a different model?
questions.expected_answer: No. Each model family trains its own tokenizer on its own vocabulary, so the same text produces a different token count on a different model — always count with the tokenizer for the model you're actually using.

questions.question: My migrations are stuck in a bad state in development — what's the safe way to reset?
questions.expected_source_section: "alembic upgrade head fails with 'table already exists' — how do I reset?"
questions.expected_answer: In development it's safe to nuke the volume and start clean: docker compose down -v (removes the MySQL volume), then docker compose up --build, then docker compose run --rm backend alembic upgrade head again. Don't do this against anything with data you care about — -v is destructive.

questions.question: What's the actual difference between CLAUDE.md and .claude/settings.json?
questions.expected_source_section: "What's the actual difference between CLAUDE.md and .claude/settings.json?"
questions.expected_answer: CLAUDE.md is prose, auto-loaded at session start, for codebase overview/conventions/behavioral rules. .claude/settings.json is structured config — permissions, hooks, environment variables. There's no 'rules' field in settings.json; behavioral rules always belong in CLAUDE.md prose.

questions.question: What's the best pizza topping?
questions.notes: Deliberately out-of-scope — nothing in the ingested content is relevant. A correctly-configured pipeline should return matched: false, not a forced guess. Mirrors Lecture 13's own end-to-end test.
